# INTERIM REPORT OF GRAM-POSITIVE BACILLI
There are three typical morphologies (1)large and regular, (2)medium sized and variable, and (3)small and pleomorphic.  The large, uniformly rod-shaped Gram-positive bacilli are usually Bacillus spp. (aerobic) or Clostridium species (anaerobic).  Bacillus spp. include Bacillus subtilis (usually a contaminant), Bacillus cereus, and Bacillus anthracis.  Medium-sized Gram-positive bacilli are usually Lactobacilli (anaerobic).  Small and pleomorphic bacilli are usually Listeria (aerobic), diphtheroids (aerobic), Propionibacteria (anaerobic), and Corynebacteria (aerobic).
